title: Integrated controlbook: RBAC & auth, audit logging, data residency & retention, secure SDLC, incident response, compliance evidence, risk & exceptions
author: Amina Shah
summary: Consolidated controlbook describing Redwood Inference's policies and operational procedures for RBAC and authentication, audit logging, data residency and retention, secure SDLC practices, incident response security procedures, compliance evidence workflows, and handling risk & exceptions.
body:
Purpose
This document describes the required controls, operational runbooks, and evidence workflows used by Redwood Inference to meet internal security objectives and external compliance obligations (SOC2, ISO27001, customer contractual requirements). It is intended for engineering leads, security engineers, product owners, and auditors.

Scope
Applies to: hosted API, Redwood Dedicated control plane, Private deployments (VPC/on-prem packaging), and all internal systems that store, process, or transmit customer data or credentials. Notable exclusions: purely personal developer laptops except where used for production access (see device policy).

1) RBAC and Authentication
Overview:
- Principle: least privilege by default; role-based access with temporary elevation paths for operational tasks.
- Identity sources: Okta OIDC (primary), GSuite SAML for legacy service accounts, and an internal service account registry for non-human principals.

Roles & Role Mapping:
- admin (full org-level config, billing, IAM) - limited to small set of SRE and security staff.
- infra-engineer (create/modify infra resources, deploy) - scoped to cloud accounts and terraform state.
- platform-engineer (service-level config, model-serving rollout) - scoped to Redwood control plane resources.
- developer (code push to non-prod, feature flags, observability) - limited to dev/staging.
- support (customer support console access, redacted logs) - read-only production logs with PII redaction.
- auditor (read-only access to audit logs, compliance artifacts) - timeboxed by ticket.

Authentication & MFA:
- All human accounts require SSO via Okta and enforced MFA (TOTP + security key encouraged).
- Machine/service accounts must use short-lived credentials (OIDC workload identity) or keys stored in KMS/HSM and rotated automatically.

Provisioning & Deprovisioning:
1. New hires: access requested in Okta request workflow; manager approval required; least-privilege role assigned by default.
2. Leavers: automated deprovisioning via HR signal; cloud access revoked within 4 hours of termination signal (SLO).
3. Emergency access: documented temporary escalation process using Just-In-Time (JIT) elevation with 1-hour expiry and full audit.

Periodic Reviews:
- Quarterly role membership review owned by security (owner: Identity and Access team).
- Access reviews for high-privilege roles monthly.

2) Audit Logging
Goals:
- Provide immutable record of authentication, authorization decisions, admin console actions, infra changes (Terraform apply), and customer-facing request metadata required for incident investigation and compliance evidence.

Log Collection & Retention:
- Central logging pipeline: Fluentd -> Kafka -> S3 (immutable) + Elasticsearch for 90-day fast query.
- WORM/Evidence store: logs relevant to compliance (auth events, admin changes, security incidents) are copied to the Evidence bucket with object lock for required retention windows.

Minimum log fields (every event):
- timestamp, event_id, principal_id, principal_type (human/service), action, resource, result (success/failure), request_id, trace_id, ip_address, user_agent, change_summary

Sample audit event (JSON):
```json
{
  "timestamp": "2026-02-18T14:22:31Z",
  "event_id": "evt_0a1b2c3d",
  "principal_id": "user:dp-park@redwoodai.com",
  "principal_type": "human",
  "action": "iam.role.assign",
  "resource": "org:root/role:admin",
  "result": "success",
  "request_id": "req_9f8e7d6c",
  "trace_id": "trace-12345",
  "ip_address": "198.51.100.22",
  "user_agent": "Okta-SSO/1.0",
  "change_summary": "Assigned admin role for quarterly ops" 
}
```

Log Integrity & Access:
- All write-once logs have SHA256 checksums and are stored with object-lock and server-side encryption (KMS).
- Only security and SRE have read access to the raw evidence bucket; auditors get timeboxed access through ticketing.

3) Data Residency & Retention
Policy summary:
- Customer data is stored only in customer-selected regions for Redwood Dedicated and Private deployments. For hosted API, customers may choose region at account creation; default is us-west-2.
- Data classification: PII, customer-generated content, system telemetry, secret material.

Retention matrix (minimums):
| Data type | Short-term store | Backup/Evidence store | Retention period |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Authentication events | 90 days (ES) | 7 years (Evidence bucket) | 7 years |
| Customer request logs (non-PII) | 90 days | 1 year | 1 year |
| Customer request logs (contains PII) | 90 days (redacted index) | 7 years (encrypted evidence) | 7 years or per contract |
| Model artifacts | 2 years | N/A (customer-managed for private) | 2 years |

Deletion & Data Subject Requests (DSR):
1. DSRs are handled through the Privacy team ticketing workflow; production data deletions are performed with job idempotency and documented snapshots.
2. Retention overrides for legal hold: Legal may request an evidence hold; hold supersedes automated deletion until rescinded.

4) Secure SDLC (Secure Software Development Lifecycle)
Principles:
- Shift-left security: threat modeling and security requirements occur before feature design phases.
- Automated gates: linting, secret-scan, dependency checks, SCA, and SAST in CI.

Minimum required checks in CI/CD:
- Unit & integration tests (required)
- Dependency vulnerability scan (Snyk or OSS alternative) - block on critical/urgent vulnerabilities
- Secret scanning (git-secrets, TruffleHog) - block on secrets in commit history
- Static analysis for common languages (Go, Python, Java) - security warnings triaged within 5 business days
- Container image vulnerability scanning and CIS benchmark check before push to registry

Pre-release requirements:
1. Threat model update for changes affecting data flow or auth boundaries.
2. Security review for high-scope features (exposes new endpoints, changes data retention).
3. Staged rollout: canary -> 5% -> 25% -> 100% with automatic rollback on error budget breach.

Developer guidance snippet (example):
```bash
# Run local pre-commit checks
make precommit
# Run SAST locally
sast-scan --path=./pkg --output=sast-report.json
```

5) Incident Response \u2014 Security Procedures
Detection & Triage:
- All potential security incidents should be reported to the security on-call via PagerDuty (tag: security-incident).
- Initial triage must classify the incident within 60 minutes (SLO).

Containment & Eradication (high level):
1. Isolate impacted resources (network ACLs, revoke compromised keys, suspend service accounts).
2. Snapshot evidence (logs, memory, disk) and copy to evidence bucket with preservation metadata.
3. Remove root cause (patch, config change) and validate fix in staging where possible.

Notification & Escalation:
- Notify stakeholders per severity matrix. See severity table below.
- External notifications (customers, regulators) coordinated by Legal and Customer Success.

Severity matrix (summary):
- Sev 1: Active exfiltration of customer data or production compromise \u2014 Pager, all hands, regulator notification as required.
- Sev 2: Degraded security posture without evidence of exfiltration \u2014 Pager to on-call, scoped incident response.
- Sev 3: Suspected vulnerability or low-impact misconfiguration \u2014 Ticket, business hours triage.

Post-incident:
- Conduct blameless postmortem within 7 business days for Sev1/2; publish findings and remediation plan.
- Update threat models and CI gates if required.

6) Compliance Evidence Workflows
Evidence categories:
- Operational evidence: runbook execution logs, SLO reports, backup run reports.
- Technical evidence: IAM role bindings, audit logs, encryption config, key rotation records.
- Organizational evidence: policies, training rosters, HR onboarding/offboarding logs.

Evidence collection process (high level):
1. Evidence capture agents (log exporter, terraform state snapshots, backups) run daily.
2. Evidence bundling service compiles artifacts, signs bundles (SHA256), and stores in Evidence WORM bucket.
3. Evidence retention and access governed via ticketing; auditors request bundles using compliance-ticket tool.

Sample compliance request procedure:
1. Auditor opens compliance ticket via internal portal with requested date range and artifact types.
2. Security reviews scope, requests timeboxed access or prepares evidence bundle.
3. Bundle is exported to a secure, read-only link with 30-day expiry unless extended by contract.

7) Risk & Exceptions
Exception process:
- All deviations from this controlbook must follow a documented exception request. Exception requests include description, risk assessment, compensating controls, expiration date, and approval path.
- Approval levels: security manager (low risk, up to 30 days), security director (medium risk, up to 6 months), CISO (high risk or >6 months).

Compensating controls examples:
- If long-lived keys are temporarily required for a migration, require IP allowlist, timeboxed credential validity, recorded video sign-off, and continuous auditing of the usage.

Risk acceptance criteria:
- Residual risk documented, compensating controls in place and tested, and business justification provided. All accepted risks are tracked in the Risk Register and reviewed at quarterly GRC meetings.

8) Ownership, SLAs, and Reporting
- Identity & Access team: owner for RBAC and deprovisioning workflows.
- Observability team: owner for logging pipeline and retention.
- Privacy team: DSR handling and data classification ownership.
- Security on-call: incident triage and evidence preservation.

Operational SLAs (selected):
- Deprovisioning on termination: 4 hours (SLO).
- Initial incident triage: 60 minutes.
- Audit evidence delivery for routine compliance request: 10 business days.

Appendix
- Useful commands and locations:
  - Evidence bucket (read-only for auditors): s3://redwood-evidence-prod (access via signed link only)
  - Audit log schema: internal wiki link (see related_pages)
  - Identity management: Okta org URL (internal)

Change history:
- 2025-09-15: Document created by Amina Shah.
- 2026-02-20: Expanded evidence workflow, updated retention matrix, tightened deprovisioning SLOs.

Contact & escalation
For questions or exceptions, file a ticket in the Security queue or email security@redwood.ai.
